title_en: Qingdao Zhongjin Yuneng Real Estate Co., Ltd. v. Qingdao Zhongjin Industrial Co., Ltd. and Binzhou Zhongjin Haoyun Real Estate Co., Ltd. — dispute over liability for damages from property preservation
ruling_gist_en: Compensation for errors in applying for property preservation is, in nature, a tort liability. To determine whether an application for property preservation is erroneous, it is necessary not only to consider whether the claim of the applicant for preservation is ultimately supported, but also to examine whether the applicant acted with intent or gross negligence. To determine whether the applicant for preservation acted with intent or gross negligence, it is necessary to assess the reasonableness of the lawsuit filed by the applicant based on the claims and the facts and grounds on which they are based, or to assess the appropriateness of the application for property preservation based on the amount, object, and method of the preservation applied for. Regarding the determination of the amount of compensation, if the preservation involves freezing of funds, and there is evidence such as a contract proving the loss of loan interest, the actual loss to be compensated is the loss of interest agreed upon in the contract; however, the sum of this interest loss and the bank interest on the frozen funds shall not exceed the upper limit of 24% per annum stipulated in the Judicial Interpretation on Private Lending; otherwise, the compensation for the loss of interest on funds shall be determined by reference to the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period or the standard of 6% per annum stipulated in the Judicial Interpretation on Private Lending. If the preservation involves the seizure of houses or other assets subject to market value fluctuations, and the preserved party does not request the disposal and realization of the assets or the request is improper and not granted, the risk of value depreciation due to market changes shall be borne by the preserved party itself, and there is no direct causal relationship with the act of applying for property preservation. If the applicant for preservation obstructs the preserved party from exercising the right of disposal, the value depreciation of the preserved property is directly causally related to the act of the applicant for preservation, and the amount to be compensated by the applicant for preservation shall be the price difference of the preserved property between the commencement and conclusion of the preservation, plus the loss of interest on the funds corresponding to the value at the commencement of the preservation. For property preservation.

full_text_en:
Qingdao Zhongjin Yuneng Real Estate Co., Ltd. v.
Qingdao Zhongjin Industrial Co., Ltd. and Binzhou Zhongjin Haoyun Real Estate
Co., Ltd. — dispute over liability for damage caused by property preservation

Ruling Summary

Compensation for errors in applying for property preservation is in the nature of tort liability. To determine whether an application for property preservation is erroneous, it is necessary to consider not only whether the applicant's claims are ultimately upheld, but also whether the applicant acted with intent or gross negligence. To determine whether the applicant acted with intent or caused significant loss, it is necessary to examine whether the lawsuit filed by the applicant was reasonable based on the claims and the facts and reasons relied upon, or to examine whether the application for property preservation was appropriate in light of the amount, object, and method of the preservation sought. Regarding the determination of the amount of compensation: if the preservation involves the freezing of funds and there is evidence such as a contract proving the loss of loan interest, the actual loss to be compensated shall be the interest loss as stipulated in the contract; however, the sum of such interest loss and the bank interest on the frozen funds shall not exceed the upper limit of 24% per annum as prescribed in the Judicial Interpretation on Private Lending; otherwise, the compensation for the interest loss on the funds shall be determined by reference to the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period or the standard of 6% per annum as stipulated in the Judicial Interpretation on Private Lending. If the preservation involves the sealing up of houses or other assets with market value fluctuations, where the preserved party fails to request the disposal and realization of the assets or the request is improperly made and not granted, the risk of value depreciation of the preserved assets due to market changes shall be borne by the preserved party itself, and there is no direct causal relationship with the act of applying for property preservation. If the applicant obstructs the preserved party from exercising the right of disposal, then the depreciation in value of the preserved assets has a direct causal relationship with the act of the applicant, and the amount of compensation to be paid by the applicant shall be the price difference of the preserved assets between the commencement and the end of the preservation, plus the loss of interest on the funds equivalent to the price at the commencement. The guarantee provided for property preservation is a judicial guarantee, and the third party shall bear liability within the scope of its guarantee commitment, rather than be jointly and severally liable for joint tort.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court
(2017) Supreme People's Court Final Civil No. 118

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Qingdao Zhongjin Industrial Co., Ltd., domiciled at Floor 10, Times Plaza, No. 52 Hong Kong Middle Road, Shinan District, Qingdao City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Si Rongbin, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Guan Haiqing, Attorney at Shandong Yingtao Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Li Chunchao, Attorney at Shandong Yingtao Law Firm.

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Binzhou Zhongjin Haoyun Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 688 Bohai 17th Road, Binzhou City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Tian Weiguo, General Manager.

Agent ad litem: Sun Wenxue, Attorney at Shandong Qiying Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Wang Caixia, Attorney at Shandong Huanzhou Law Firm.

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance): Qingdao Zhongjin Yuneng Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at Floor 18, Block A, Sunshine Tower, No. 61 Hong Kong Middle Road, Shinan District, Qingdao City, Shandong Province.

Legal Representative: Yang Bin, Chairman of the Board.

Agent ad litem: Yang Ming, Attorney at Beijing Weiheng Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Hu Xiaoxin, Attorney at Beijing Weiheng Law Firm.

In the case concerning a dispute over liability for damage caused by an application for litigation property preservation, the appellants, Qingdao Zhongjin Industrial Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongjin Industrial Company) and Binzhou Zhongjin Haoyun Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongjin Haoyun Company), appealed against the civil judgment (2014) Lu Min Yi Chong Chu Zi No. 1 of the Shandong High People's Court to this Court. This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law and held a public hearing. Guan Haiqing, agent ad litem of Zhongjin Industrial Company, Sun Wenxue and Sun Jiale (later changed to Wang Caixia after the hearing), agents ad litem of Zhongjin Haoyun Company, and Yang Ming and Hu Xiaoxin, agents ad litem of Qingdao Yuneng Company, appeared in court. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

Zhongjin Industrial Company appealed for the following: to set aside the judgment of the first instance, dismiss all claims of Qingdao Yuneng Company; and to have Qingdao Yuneng Company bear all litigation costs and preservation fees.

Facts and Reasons: First, whether Zhongjin Industrial Company should be liable for compensation mainly depends on whether Zhongjin Industrial Company acted maliciously in the process of litigation property preservation and whether the preservation act was illegal. The civil judgment (2015) Lu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 39 of the Shandong High People's Court supported Zhongjin Industrial Company's claim for share repurchase, which shows that Zhongjin Industrial Company's preservation act was not at fault, without any subjective malice or illegality. If the final judgment in that case supports Zhongjin Industrial Company's claims, the relationship between the parties in this case will become that of parent company and subsidiary, rendering the dispute in this case meaningless. Second, even if Zhongjin Industrial Company is found to have illegally sealed assets, since RMB 120 million in the sealed account still generates interest, the first instance judgment ordering Zhongjin Industrial Company to bear the loss of loan interest on RMB 120 million lacks factual and legal basis; because housing sale proceeds cannot be fully controlled by Qingdao Yuneng Company, even if kept in the account, the interest would be deposit interest, so the first instance judgment's support for loan interest is clearly contrary to legal principle. The case should await the final judgment in the (2015) Lu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 39 case of the Shandong High People's Court, and therefore Zhongjin Industrial Company applies for a stay of proceedings in this case. In addition, after the hearing, Zhongjin Industrial Company submitted an "Application for Adding Parties to the Litigation," requesting that China Railway Properties Group Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as China Railway Company) and Qingdao Rongzhidi Consulting Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Rongzhidi Company) be added as defendants or third parties in this case.

Zhongjin Haoyun Company appealed for the following: to set aside the judgment of the first instance, to modify the judgment so that Zhongjin Haoyun Company does not bear joint and several compensation liability, and to have Qingdao Yuneng Company bear all litigation costs of the first instance and the appeal and preservation fees.

Facts and Reasons: First, Zhongjin Industrial Company's application for preservation was not at fault and does not constitute an erroneous application for preservation. Zhongjin Industrial Company's filing of the lawsuit, amendment of claims, and application for property preservation were all to protect its own lawful rights and interests. There was no subjective intent or gross negligence in erroneously applying for preservation to harm Qingdao Yuneng Company's lawful rights and interests. The first instance court's finding that the preservation was erroneous solely because Zhongjin Industrial Company's claims were not supported lacks factual and legal basis. The first instance court, when ordering the sealing, failed to verify the true value of the preserved assets, leading to a serious excess of the amount to be preserved, which violates legal provisions and infringes upon the lawful rights and interests of Qingdao Yuneng Company. Making Zhongjin Haoyun Company pay for such illegal acts goes against the pursuit of fairness and justice. Second, there is no causal relationship between Zhongjin Industrial Company's application for property preservation and the losses claimed by Qingdao Yuneng Company. 1. Qingdao Yuneng Company failed to exercise its right to apply for reconsideration of the preservation in a timely manner, and did not take measures such as requesting a swap of the sealed land for a freeze on the sales fund account to reduce losses, thereby constituting major fault. 2. The value of the sealed land fully covered the frozen amount of RMB 120 million, and Qingdao Yuneng Company was at fault for not timely applying for the release of the freeze. 3. Qingdao Yuneng Company's sales situation was affected by various factors, including local policies and its own major disputes, and had no direct relationship with Zhongjin Industrial Company's application for property preservation. Third, Zhongjin Industrial Company's application for property preservation did not cause actual losses to Qingdao Yuneng Company, and the first instance judgment lacks a sufficient basis. 1. The property losses compensated by the tortfeasor should be certain or necessarily occur in the future. Given the continuously rising property prices in Qingdao since 2011, delaying the sale of Qingdao Yuneng Company's properties did not result in losses but could have even generated profits. 2. The first instance judgment's discretionary determination of one year's interest loss based on 10% of total sales proceeds exceeds the scope of evidence provided by Qingdao Yuneng Company and seriously contradicts the facts proved by the notarized documents submitted by Qingdao Yuneng Company. 3. There was no interest loss on the frozen RMB 120 million; even if it existed, it was due to Qingdao Yuneng Company's fault in not applying for the release of the freeze, and because it involved illegal lending, the interest should be confiscated; otherwise, the deposit interest during the freeze period should be deducted according to the principle of offsetting gains and losses. Fourth, Zhongjin Haoyun Company's provision of a guarantee for its shareholder's property preservation was not approved by a shareholders' meeting, rendering the guarantee void. Even if liability is to be borne, it should be limited to the property provided as a guarantee, not joint and several guarantee liability. The first instance judgment's ruling that Zhongjin Haoyun Company bears joint and several compensation liability on the ground of joint tort is erroneous in the application of law.

Qingdao Yuneng Company argued in defense that all appeal requests of Zhongjin Industrial Company and Zhongjin Haoyun Company lack factual and legal basis and should be dismissed.

Facts and Reasons: First, the first instance judgment's finding that Zhongjin Industrial Company's application for preservation was erroneous has a sufficient factual and legal basis. 1. As determined on pages 4 and 5 of the Supreme People's Court's Civil Judgment (2011) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 108, a series of actions by Zhongjin Industrial Company in the project's sales pricing decision process prove that Zhongjin Industrial Company's purpose in applying for preservation was to prevent the normal sale of the project by sealing up the land use right of Qingdao Yuneng Company. 2. Qingdao Yuneng Company repeatedly provided equity and property as guarantees to unseal the project land use right, but Zhongjin Industrial Company constantly increased the amount of the claim and the preservation limit without basis to obstruct. In the original trial, Zhongjin Industrial Company even claimed that it had originally planned to name Qingdao Yuneng Company as a third party but listed it as a defendant to achieve the preservation of the project land use right. Zhongjin Industrial Company always sought the result of the land use right being sealed, showing extremely serious subjective fault. Second, the first instance judgment's discretionary determination of one year's interest loss based on 10% of total sales proceeds is still far lower than the actual loss. 1. The interest loss caused by the erroneous preservation application preventing project sales was at least RMB 189,553,873.10. 2. Zhongjin Industrial Company's argument that the first instance judgment's discretionary determination of one year's interest loss based on 10% of total sales proceeds is too high is without any basis. 3. Zhongjin Industrial Company's argument that the project could not have been sold even without the sealing contradicts its own reasons for opposing the low sales pricing and does not match the actual sales situation of surrounding projects. Third, several reasons by Zhongjin Industrial Company that the first instance judgment's interest loss on the frozen RMB 120 million is erroneous are all unfounded. The funds raised by Qingdao Yuneng Company from its shareholders are lawful loans under the Judicial Interpretation on Private Lending; the first instance judgment's calculation based on the loan interest rate half a year earlier is already far lower than the actual cost of funds. Fourth, Zhongjin Haoyun Company's accusation that "the respondent failed to take proper and effective measures and was itself grossly negligent" is completely contrary to the facts. Qingdao Yuneng Company, when the project met sales conditions, had to recover funds through project sales to alleviate huge financial pressure and comply with government requirements against hoarding properties for higher prices. Zhongjin Haoyun Company's argument that there was no need to raise RMB 120 million to unseal the land use right is completely unfounded. After Qingdao Yuneng Company raised RMB 120 million and just unsealed the land use right, Zhongjin Industrial Company and Zhongjin Haoyun Company increased the preservation amount and provided new guarantees to seal again. Given their approach of not stopping until they achieved their goal of blocking project sales, there was no possibility of reconsideration or swapping the seal. Fifth, Zhongjin Industrial Company and Zhongjin Haoyun Company's shifting of their own erroneous preservation responsibility to the court is without basis. Zhongjin Industrial Company and Zhongjin Haoyun Company, to prevent the normal sale of the project, arbitrarily changed their claims and preservation requests five times, which is a typical abuse of procedural rights. Their accusation that the court illegally exceeded the preservation amount is essentially an attempt to shift responsibility. Sixth, China Railway Company and Rongzhidi Company are unrelated to the dispute in this case. Zhongjin Industrial Company's application to add these two companies as defendants or third parties in this case in its appeal brief lacks factual and legal basis. Seventh, losses such as liability for breach of contract towards construction parties, lending banks, and suppliers due to the inability to sell the project in time, as well as price reduction losses, objectively existed. The first instance judgment's discretionary award of RMB 66,694,625.35 in losses accounts for only a small portion of the total losses. Qingdao Yuneng Company, to avoid prolonged litigation and obtain compensation as soon as possible, chose to respect and comply with the first instance judgment.

Claims of Qingdao Yuneng Company at First Instance: First, Zhongjin Industrial Company shall compensate Qingdao Yuneng Company for losses of RMB 193,063,873.10 caused by the erroneous application for property preservation; second, Zhongjin Haoyun Company and Zhongjin Industrial Company shall bear joint and several compensation liability to Qingdao Yuneng Company for the losses of RMB 193,063,873.10 caused by the erroneous property preservation.

Facts Found by the First Instance Court: On September 22, 2005, Qingdao Yuneng Company was registered and established with the Shinan Branch of the Qingdao Administration for Industry and Commerce. Its company type is a limited liability company, a legal entity, with a business scope including real estate development and sales. The "Qingdao International Trade Center" project involved in this case was developed and constructed by it.

On April 3, 2008, to resolve the project's capital shortage, the shareholders of Qingdao Yuneng Company — Chongqing Yuneng Industry Co., Ltd., Shandong Jide Ecological Technology Co., Ltd., Zhongjin Industrial Company, China Railway Company, and Qingdao Yuneng Company — signed a "Framework Cooperation Agreement." The agreement stipulated that Chongqing Yuneng Industry Co., Ltd., Shandong Jide Ecological Technology Co., Ltd., and Zhongjin Industrial Company agreed to transfer their respective 50%, 24.5%, and 17.5% equity interests in Qingdao Yuneng Company to China Railway Company. China Railway Company would invest in Qingdao Yuneng Company through foreign capital, engage in the development and operation of the project, and enjoy the benefits from project sales.

On April 13 and May 9, 2008, China Railway Company (Party A), Zhongjin Industrial Company (Party B), and Qingdao Yuneng Company (Party C) entered into a "Supplementary Agreement" and an "Investment Cooperation Agreement" respectively regarding the specific cooperation matters of the project. Article 5 of the "Investment Cooperation Agreement" provided that Party A's investment in the company was a strategic investment and a temporary shareholding. After Party A recovered its investment (excluding equity investment) and returns, it agreed that Party B could repurchase Party A's equity in the company. Article 7 provided that once the project met pre-sale conditions, the company would commence sales. The proceeds from sales would first be used to repay Party A's investment principal and returns. This article also provided that investment returns would be calculated annually, at 30% of the total investment amount actually used by the company in that year, and would be settled and paid before December 20 of that year. Article 8 stipulated the conditions for Party B to repurchase all of Party A's equity in the company. The repurchase consideration would be calculated as Party A's equity investment amount plus an annual premium of 30% on the equity investment amount. Party B's repurchase of all of Party A's equity should occur within five years after the signing of the agreement. Article 11(5) provided that, during the project's development and operation, for activities other than asset disposal, equity transfer, and external guarantees, Party A had the right to decide independently, but Party B had the right to be informed. In addition, Party B had the right to provide marketing and sales plans for the project, but the final plan must be approved by the company's board of directors. Article 11(6) provided that to ensure the smooth progress of the various content under this agreement, if one party encountered an obligation of assistance, the other party should actively assist and cooperate. Article 12 provided that each party should fully perform its respective obligations in accordance with the agreement; if one party breached the contract and caused losses to other parties, it should compensate the other parties for the corresponding losses.

After the signing of the above agreements, Qingdao Yuneng Company held a shareholders' meeting, approved the equity transfer as agreed, and passed an amendment to the articles of association. The shareholders of Qingdao Yuneng Company changed to China Railway Company (capital contribution of RMB 92 million) and Zhongjin Industrial Company (capital contribution of RMB 8 million). In the amendment to the articles of association, the provision of Article 28 of the original articles of association regarding "the distribution of company profits shall be implemented in accordance with the Company Law and relevant laws, regulations, and regulations of the financial department under the State Council" was also deleted.

Subsequently, China Railway Company began to intervene in Qingdao Yuneng Company, successively investing and raising funds, promoting the development and construction of the project. On March 31, 2010, Qingdao Yuneng Company signed a "Sales Agency Contract for the Qingdao Center Project" with Rongzhidi Company, entrusting Rongzhidi Company to sell the project. On January 19, 2011, Qingdao Yuneng Company held a board of directors meeting to consider the pricing strategy plan for the Qingdao International Trade Center project. The meeting ultimately approved the pricing strategy plan with four out of five directors in favor and one against (Zhongjin Industrial Company), while also instructing the company's management to handle the pre-sale permit and authorizing them to determine the timing of the launch. On March 7, 2011, Qingdao Yuneng Company obtained a pre-sale permit for the Qingdao International Trade Center. In its filed commercial housing pre-sale plan, the prices for the pre-sold residential units were as follows: average price for residential units was RMB 41,111/square meter, average price for office units was RMB 41,637/square meter, average price for commercial units was RMB 73,371/square meter, and average price for serviced apartments was RMB 36,667/square meter.

On January 24, 2011, Zhongjin Industrial Company filed a lawsuit against China Railway Company, Qingdao Yuleng Company, and Rongzhidi Company as defendants, alleging that on May 9, 2008, Zhongjin Industrial Company, China Railway Company, and Qingdao Yuleng Company entered into an "Investment Cooperation Agreement." Pursuant to this agreement, upon the satisfaction of the repurchase conditions, Zhongjin Industrial Company had the right to repurchase from China Railway Company the 92% equity interest that China Railway Company held in Qingdao Yuleng Company, and prior to the satisfaction of the repurchase conditions, Zhongjin Industrial Company had the right to introduce a strategic investor to acquire a certain percentage of equity from China Railway Company. Zhongjin Industrial Company enjoyed the rights to repurchase equity and introduce a strategic investor. On July 9, 2010, Zhongjin Industrial Company sent a letter to China Railway Company and Qingdao Yuleng Company requesting cooperation in the equity repurchase, requiring them to initiate the corresponding equity repurchase procedures. China Railway Company and Qingdao Yuleng Company refused to cooperate in satisfying the equity repurchase conditions, maliciously obstructed the satisfaction of the conditions, and seriously breached the obligation of "active assistance and cooperation" as stipulated in Article 11 of the Investment Cooperation Agreement. Moreover, the satisfaction of the equity repurchase conditions required the assistance and cooperation of both China Railway Company and Qingdao Yuleng Company. China Railway Company and Qingdao Yuleng Company maliciously obstructed the satisfaction of the equity repurchase conditions, and in accordance with the Contract Law of the PRC, the conditions should be deemed to have been satisfied. Furthermore, Zhongjin Industrial Company had already made a repurchase request on July 9, 2010, but it could not be completed solely because China Railway Company and Qingdao Yuleng Company refused to cooperate. China Railway Company was no longer entitled to the annual investment return rate after July 9. After the Investment Cooperation Agreement was signed, China Railway Company, taking advantage of its status as a temporary shareholder, misappropriated project company funds amounting to RMB 1.2 billion; maliciously engaged in internal sales at prices below market value, causing RMB 1.8 billion in losses to Zhongjin Industrial Company; forcibly halted the project, causing daily losses of millions of yuan; and unilaterally used RMB 120 million in cash from the project company to provide guarantees. These actions seriously violated the provisions of Article 11 of the Investment Cooperation Agreement, and China Railway Company should be liable for compensating Zhongjin Industrial Company for the losses suffered. Zhongjin Industrial Company therefore requested the court to order: 1. That Zhongjin Industrial Company has the right to repurchase equity, provided that China Railway Company performs its obligations of assistance and cooperation as agreed in the contract; 2. That China Railway Company and Qingdao Yuleng Company cooperate with Zhongjin Industrial Company in achieving the equity repurchase conditions set forth in Article 8(2) of the Investment Cooperation Agreement as of the date of the request (June 29, 2011); 3. That China Railway Company and Qingdao Yuleng Company assist Zhongjin Industrial Company in undergoing industrial and commercial registration changes to transfer the 92% equity held in the name of China Railway Company to Zhongjin Industrial Company or a third-party strategic investor designated by Zhongjin Industrial Company; 4. That the 30% annual investment return rate enjoyed by China Railway Company under the Investment Cooperation Agreement be calculated up to July 9, 2010; 5. That the defendants immediately cease any form of malicious disposal actions against the project (including but not limited to sales, suspension of construction, mortgages, fund appropriation, etc.) and bear the resulting losses of approximately RMB 3 billion, provisionally claimed at RMB 480 million (after multiple amendments), subject to court verification; and 6. That all litigation, audit, appraisal, and preservation costs be borne by China Railway Company and Qingdao Yuleng Company.

On January 26, 2011, upon the application of Zhongjin Industrial Company, the Shandong High People's Court issued Civil Ruling (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2-1, ordering property preservation against Qingdao Yuleng Company's assets. Zhongjin Haoyun Company provided as security a property located at No. 192, New Capital World Trade Square, South of Huanghe 7th Road, East of Bohai 17th Road, Binzhou City, Shandong Province, registered in its name. On January 28, 2011, the court actually sealed the land use rights of the Qingdao International Trade Center project developed by Qingdao Yuleng Company. To lift the seal and ensure the normal sale of the project, Qingdao Yuleng Company raised RMB 120 million in deposits from China Railway Company as security and applied to lift the above-mentioned seal. On February 23, 2011, the court issued Civil Ruling (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2-3, lifting the seal on the land use rights of the Qingdao International Trade Center project and simultaneously freezing RMB 120 million in deposits of Qingdao Yuleng Company. On March 7, 2011, Qingdao Yuleng Company obtained the commercial housing pre-sale permit. On February 25, 2011, Zhongjin Industrial Company increased the subject matter of its claim to RMB 240 million and continued to apply for property preservation against Qingdao Yuleng Company, with Zhongjin Haoyun Company continuing to provide security using its correspondingly valued properties. On March 2, 2011, the court issued Civil Ruling (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2-5, ordering the sealing of the land use rights of the Qingdao International Trade Center project owned by Qingdao Yuleng Company. On March 9, 2011, the court actually sealed the land use rights of the Qingdao International Trade Center project. Thereafter, Zhongjin Industrial Company repeatedly amended its claims and applied to increase the amount of property preservation. As of June 29, 2011, Zhongjin Industrial Company ultimately increased the amount of claimed economic loss compensation to RMB 480 million. With the support of the guarantee from Zhongjin Haoyun Company, on September 8, 2011, the court issued Civil Ruling (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2-8, raising the limit of property preservation against Qingdao Yuleng Company to RMB 390 million.

On September 13, 2011, the Shandong High People's Court rendered Civil Judgment (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2, dismissing all of Zhongjin Industrial Company's claims on the ground of insufficient evidence. Zhongjin Industrial Company appealed to the Supreme People's Court. On March 15, 2012, the Supreme People's Court, in its Civil Judgment (2011) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 108, dismissed Zhongjin Industrial Company's appeal.

On April 10, 2012, upon the application of China Railway Company and Qingdao Yuleng Company, the Shandong High People's Court issued Civil Ruling (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2-11, lifting the seal on the land use rights of Qingdao Yuleng Company's Qingdao International Trade Center project and unfreezing account No. 236400406456 of Qingdao Yuleng Company held at the Shandong Provincial Branch of Bank of China Co., Ltd.

On October 26, 2010, the Shandong Provincial Branch of Bank of China Co., Ltd. issued a certificate to the Qingdao Real Estate Registration Center, stating that the Qingdao International Trade Center project developed by Qingdao Yuleng Company, located at No. 8B, Hong Kong Middle Road, Shinan District, Qingdao City, had a planned total investment of RMB 4.18 billion (excluding land costs). Construction funds invested in the project at that time amounted to RMB 855.92 million (excluding land costs), including: preliminary engineering costs of RMB 245.3 million, construction and installation engineering costs of RMB 1,048.53 million, and development overhead costs of RMB 562.09 million, accounting for 44% of the total investment. On the same day, the South Second Sub-branch of Qingdao, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Co., Ltd. issued a certificate stating that the Qingdao International Trade Center project developed by Qingdao Yuleng Company, located at No. 8B, Hong Kong Middle Road, Shinan District, Qingdao City, under Land Certificate No. Qing Fang Di Quan Shi Zi 201065164, had its use rights mortgaged to the bank, which was a land mortgage (the mortgage scope did not include public supporting facilities). The bank agreed that the company could apply for the pre-sale permit and sell to the public. On the same day, the South Sub-branch of Qingdao, Agricultural Bank of China Co., Ltd. also issued a certificate identical to that of the South Second Sub-branch of Qingdao, Industrial and Commercial Bank of China Co., Ltd. On March 7, 2011, Qingdao Yuleng Company obtained the Qingdao Commercial Housing Pre-sale Permit No. Qing Fang Zhu Zi (2011) 009. The permit listed the project name as Qingdao International Trade Center, located at Buildings 1-3, Wu, Ji, No. 8B, Hong Kong Middle Road, Shinan District, with a total above-ground construction area of 212,252.80 square meters. On March 7, 2011, the commercial housing pre-sale plan prepared by Qingdao Yuleng Company stated that the total number of units for pre-sale was 656, with a pre-sale area of 212,252.80 square meters. During the period when the land use rights of the project were sealed, the commercial housing permitted for pre-sale under the pre-sale permit could not be actually sold.

On January 28, 2011, the General Office of the Qingdao Municipal People's Government issued Qing Zheng Ban Fa [2011] No. 8, "Opinions on Further Improving Real Estate Market Regulation and Promoting the Stable and Healthy Development of the Real Estate Market," deciding to implement a policy limiting the number of housing purchases and strictly restricting speculative home purchases. This policy was to implement housing purchase restriction measures in the urban area of Qingdao (seven districts under the municipal jurisdiction) from the date of issuance of the opinions until December 31, 2011.

The sales agent for the Qingdao International Trade Center project was Rongzhidi Company. On April 14, 2012, Rongzhidi Company provided Qingdao Yuleng Company with a "Forecast Report on the Sales Status of the Qingdao International Trade Center Project," which stated that if the project launched on or before January 28, 2011, the expected sales progress within one week of launch would be 22%, within one month 30%, and within one year 61%. The background at the time of launch was a good market condition, with no new competing projects on the coastal front, a healthy project image, reasonable and iconic pricing, and high customer attention and expectation. If the project launched in March 2011, the expected sales progress within one week of launch would be 17%, within one month 19%, and within one year 47%. The background at the time of launch was that the project was embroiled in litigation, its assets were sealed, causing widespread public suspicion, customers were gradually lost, and the New National Eight Regulations and the Qingdao Purchase Restriction Order were successively issued, leaving the project in an awkward position. If the project launched in March 2012, the expected sales progress within one week of launch would be 10%, within one month 13%, and within one year 30%. The background at the time of launch was that after one year of real estate market regulation, high-end property prices in Qingdao had fallen significantly, and it was no longer realistic to maintain the original sales price for the project; a reduction in sales price was recommended.

The losses claimed by Qingdao Yuleng Company consisted of interest losses of RMB 189,553,873.10 due to a half-year delay in project sales, and interest losses of RMB 3.51 million due to the freezing of RMB 120 million in funds for half a year. The calculation method was: the total value of the project after full sales was RMB 10,013,411,148.72. Based on a minimum of 30% of sales at launch, the interest loss on that amount for just one year was RMB 189,553,873.10; for the frozen RMB 120 million, calculated at the half-year loan interest rate of 5.85% (from February 23, 2011 to August 23, 2011), the interest loss was RMB 3.51 million (RMB 120 million x 5.85% x 0.5). The total of the above two items was RMB 193,063,873.10.

On December 18, 2014, the Supreme People's Court issued Civil Ruling (2013) Min Shen Zi No. 161, dismissing Zhongjin Industrial Company's application for retrial of Civil Judgment (2011) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 108.

Additionally, it was found that at the time of the application and implementation of the preservation measures in this case, the loan interest rates published by the People's Bank of China were: half-year rate 5.85%, one-year rate 6.31%.

The court of first instance held that: This case involves a dispute arising from property losses caused to the other party due to errors in the application for property preservation during litigation. In the first instance case of Shandong High People's Court (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2 and the second instance case of the Supreme People's Court (2011) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 108, Zhongjin Industrial Company and Zhongjin Haoyun Company were respectively the applicant and the guarantor of the property preservation, and Qingdao Yuleng Company was the respondent. In this case, the plaintiff and the defendants both have proper party status. There are three focal issues in this dispute: first, whether Zhongjin Industrial Company's application for preservation was erroneous; second, the determination of the amount of losses suffered by Qingdao Yuleng Company due to the erroneous application for property preservation; and third, whether Zhongjin Haoyun Company should bear joint and several liability for compensation.

Regarding the first focal issue, whether Zhongjin Industrial Company's application for preservation was erroneous. The court held that: The conduct of erroneously applying for property preservation, causing property losses to the respondent, constitutes an act under the General Principles of the Civil Law of the PRC and the Tort Law of the PRC where a person, due to fault, infringes upon another's property and shall bear civil liability according to law. Article 105 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC provides that if the application is erroneous, the applicant shall compensate the respondent for the losses suffered due to the preservation. Based on the facts found by the court, on January 28, 2011, upon the application of Zhongjin Industrial Company, in another case, the court ordered the freezing and sealing of Qingdao Yuleng Company's sales accounts and land use rights. However, the outcome of the case was that Zhongjin Industrial Company's claims were dismissed by this court and the Supreme People's Court, and its claims were not supported. Furthermore, during the implementation of the preservation measures, to ensure the normal progress of project sales, Qingdao Yuleng Company provided RMB 120 million in deposits as security, and on February 25, 2011, the preservation measures on the project's land use rights were lifted and replaced. On March 7, 2011, after Qingdao Yuleng Company obtained the commercial housing pre-sale permit, Zhongjin Industrial Company again applied to increase the preservation amount by RMB 120 million, raising the amount of property preservation against Qingdao Yuleng Company to RMB 240 million. As a result, the project for which Qingdao Yuleng Company had already obtained the pre-sale permit was once again unable to be sold due to the sealing of the land use rights. To counter Qingdao Yuleng Company's application to lift the sealing, Zhongjin Industrial Company repeatedly increased the subject matter of its claims and applied to increase the ceiling of the sealing, so that by September 8, 2011, the amount of preservation it applied for had been raised to RMB 390 million, causing the project's land use rights of Qingdao Yuleng Company to remain under sealing for more than a year, affecting the project's sales. Therefore, Zhongjin Industrial Company's application for property preservation, especially its repeated acts of increasing the preservation amount, not only exhibited subjective fault but also objectively caused economic losses to Qingdao Yuleng Company. There is a direct causal relationship between the loss and the actions of Zhongjin Industrial Company, and Zhongjin Industrial Company shall bear liability for compensation.

Regarding the second focal issue: The determination of the amount of losses suffered by Qingdao Yuleng Company due to the erroneous application for property preservation. The losses claimed by Qingdao Yuleng Company include the following two parts:

First, regarding the issue of interest loss on the frozen RMB 120 million in funds. Because Qingdao Yuleng Company's RMB 120 million in funds were frozen for half a year (from February 23, 2011 to August 23, 2011), its capital turnover was affected, causing corresponding losses. As for the defenses raised by Zhongjin Haoyun Company that the loan was an illegal loan and should be treated as deposit interest, these defenses lack both factual and legal basis and lack relevance to the loss caused by the freezing of funds. The court does not adopt them. Qingdao Yuleng Company now claims this loss based on the loan interest rate published by the People's Bank of China for the same period, and this claim should be supported. Calculated according to the half-year loan interest rate of 5.85% published by the People's Bank of China on April 6, 2011, the interest loss on the frozen RMB 120 million deposit for half a year is RMB 3.51 million (RMB 120 million x 5.85% x 0.5).

Second, regarding the interest loss due to the delayed sale of the buildings. Qingdao Yuleng Company claims compensation based on one year's interest calculated on 30% of the total expected sales amount as the amount of its loss. Since this expected sales amount is the price stated in the filed commercial housing pre-sale plan, and one of the reasons Zhongjin Industrial Company filed the lawsuit and applied for preservation was that the sale price was too low, using this sales amount as the basis for calculating the loss can reflect the market transaction price at that time and will not infringe upon the rights of Zhongjin Industrial Company. It can be used as a basis for calculating the amount of loss. Regarding the ratio for calculating the loss, based on Zhongjin Industrial Company's application, the court on January 28, 2011, ordered the sealing and freezing of relevant properties of Qingdao Yuleng Company. Since the Qingdao municipal government had already issued a policy restricting the purchase of commercial housing on January 20, 2011, the sale of residential, office, commercial, and hotel-style apartments involved in this case would inevitably be affected even without the litigation preservation. Because fluctuations in real estate prices and sales progress are heavily influenced by policy, market conditions, and other factors, and although Zhongjin Industrial Company was at fault for applying for the sealing, the filing of the lawsuit had some basis in contract and facts, and it was not a fabricated lawsuit to prevent property sales. After comprehensively considering various factors, the court determines ex aequo et bono that: the loss is to be calculated as one year's interest on 10% of the total sales amount. Calculated at the one-year bank loan interest rate of 6.31% published by the People's Bank of China for the same period, Zhongjin Industrial Company shall compensate Qingdao Yuleng Company for the interest loss on the sales proceeds due to the one-year delay in project sales, amounting to RMB 63,184,624.35 (RMB 1,639,314,102.72 x 10% x 6.31% = RMB 63,184,624.35).

In summary, Zhongjin Industrial Company shall compensate Qingdao Yuleng Company for the losses caused by the erroneous application for property preservation, totaling RMB 66,694,624.35.

Regarding the third focal issue, whether Zhongjin Haoyun Company should bear joint and several liability for compensation. Zhongjin Haoyun Company defended that its provision of security was not approved by a shareholders' meeting or board of directors' resolution, violating Article 16(2) and (3) of the Company Law of the PRC regarding the provision of guarantees by companies. Furthermore, during the provision of the guarantee, Zhongjin Industrial Company engaged in fraudulent conduct, rendering the guarantee void, and Zhongjin Haoyun Company should not bear guarantee liability. In response, the court held: According to Articles 100 and 105 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, a people's court, when taking preservation measures, may order the applicant to provide security. If the application is erroneous, the applicant and the guarantor shall compensate the respondent for losses suffered due to the preservation.

When Qingdao Yuleng Company provided secured property to request the lifting of the sealing, Zhongjin Industrial Company repeatedly increased the preservation amount, and Zhongjin Haoyun Company voluntarily increased the provision of secured property, providing security for Zhongjin Industrial Company's preservation application. According to the provisions of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC on preservation and security, Zhongjin Haoyun Company should have been aware that its provision of security could lead to compensation due to an erroneous application. The conduct of Zhongjin Haoyun Company in providing security caused the freezing of Qingdao Yuleng Company's funds and the sealing of the project's land use rights. According to Article 8 of the Tort Law of the PRC, it shall bear joint and several liability for compensation. Zhongjin Haoyun Company's defense that the provision of security violated the Company Law and that Zhongjin Industrial Company engaged in fraud pertains to issues of internal company management and the exercise of shareholders' rights. The security provided by Zhongjin Haoyun Company for the preservation was examined and accepted by the people's court, and the security is legally valid. Any dispute between Zhongjin Haoyun Company and Zhongjin Industrial Company can be resolved separately. Therefore, the court does not accept this defense of Zhongjin Haoyun Company. Zhongjin Haoyun Company shall bear joint and several liability for compensation for the losses caused by Zhongjin Industrial Company's erroneous application for preservation.

In summary, in accordance with Article 6 and Article 8 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China, and Articles 100, 105, and 152 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. Zhongjin Industrial Company shall, within ten days from the effective date of this judgment, compensate Qingdao Yuneng Company for losses of RMB 66,694,624.35 caused by the erroneous application for property preservation;

2. Zhongjin Haoyun Company shall bear joint and several liability for compensation in respect of item 1 of this judgment;

3. The other claims of Qingdao Yuneng Company are dismissed.

Court acceptance fee of RMB 1,007,119 shall be borne by Qingdao Yuneng Company in the amount of RMB 671,413, and jointly by Zhongjin Industrial Company and Zhongjin Haoyun Company in the amount of RMB 335,706; property preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne by Qingdao Yuneng Company in the amount of RMB 2,500, and jointly by Zhongjin Industrial Company and Zhongjin Haoyun Company in the amount of RMB 2,500.

Upon trial, this court affirms the facts found by the court of first instance.

During the second instance, each party submitted new evidence. Zhongjin Industrial Company submitted four pieces of new evidence: the civil judgment of Shandong High People's Court (2015) Lu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 39, the civil ruling of the Supreme People's Court (2016) Zui Gao Fa Min Zhong No. 584, the summons for trial of Shandong High People's Court, and the mediation opinion issued by Qingdao Yuneng Company during the trial of the Supreme People's Court case (2016) Zui Gao Fa Min Zhong No. 584. These were intended to prove that it had a right of repurchase over Qingdao Yuneng Company's equity, and that whether the preservation of assets in Shandong High People's Court case (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2 was erroneous should await the retrial result of Shandong High People's Court case (2015) Lu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 39, and thus the present case should be stayed. Qingdao Yuneng Company challenged the evidence, arguing that although the foregoing evidence was authentic, the determination of whether the preservation of assets in the case at issue was erroneous should be based on the outcome of the judgment in Shandong High People's Court case (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2, and had nothing to do with whether Shandong High People's Court case (2015) Lu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 39 ultimately supported Zhongjin Industrial Company's equity repurchase, and therefore the present case should not be stayed.

Zhongjin Haoyun Company submitted four pieces of new evidence: Evidence 1 and 2 were notarial certificates concerning the sales situation of the "Lu Shang Shou Fu" and "Wan Li Hai Jing" projects, and the sales situation of the project currently developed by Qingdao Yuneng Company, intended to prove that the sales volume and price determined by the court of first instance were clearly inconsistent with the facts; Evidence 3 was the Interim Measures of Qingdao Municipality for the Supervision of Pre-Sale Funds of Newly Built Commercial Housing, intended to prove that Qingdao Yuneng Company was at fault for not filing a reconsideration application to the court regarding the seizure, and even if there were seizure losses, it should bear them itself. Evidence 4 was the guarantee letter issued by Zhongjin Haoyun Company for the property preservation by Zhongjin Industrial Company and the civil rulings of Shandong High People's Court (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2 and (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2-7, intended to prove that it provided a guarantee with property of corresponding value, rather than a joint and several liability guarantee. Qingdao Yuneng Company challenged the evidence, arguing that it recognized the authenticity of the foregoing evidence but did not recognize its relevance and the purpose of proof. As to Evidence 1, Zhongjin Haoyun Company's analogy of the price and sales of the remaining unsold units or resettlement housing of other projects to the sales of the project in question was not comparable; Evidence 2 exactly proved that the preservation of assets at issue caused the project to miss the best sales opportunity, resulting in unsatisfactory sales; Evidence 3 could not prove that Qingdao Yuneng Company did not take other measures to mitigate losses; and in the three guarantee letters of Evidence 4, Zhongjin Haoyun Company all stated that if losses were caused by improper preservation of assets, it would bear corresponding liability, so Zhongjin Haoyun Company's claim that it did not bear joint and several liability was inconsistent with the facts.

Qingdao Yuneng Company submitted two pieces of new evidence: Evidence 1 was the Reconsideration Application, intended to prove that Zhongjin Haoyun Company's accusation that Qingdao Yuneng Company failed to timely file a reconsideration or apply for unsealing measures was inconsistent with the facts; Evidence 2 was the "Qingdao 'Sea View Luxury Homes' Version of Resettlement Housing Appears, Residents of Yanzidao Road Area Choose Resettlement Housing (Group Photo)", intended to prove that the sales price of the so-called Lu Shang Shou Fu provided by Zhongjin Haoyun Company was not comparable to the project in this case. Zhongjin Industrial Company challenged the evidence, arguing that Evidence 1 was a copy, and it reserved its opinion on authenticity; Evidence 2 was not notarized or verified, and its authenticity was not recognized. Zhongjin Haoyun Company challenged the evidence, arguing that it had no knowledge of Evidence 1, and even if it was authentic, it was irrelevant to its failure to timely assert rights; Evidence 2 was printed online, its authenticity could not be confirmed, and even if authentic, the information showed resettlement housing, which did not correspond to the sales price of commercial housing submitted by Zhongjin Haoyun Company.

As to whether the aforementioned new evidence submitted by the parties during the second instance should be admitted as the basis for finding facts in this case, this court will comment on it together later.

This court holds that, based on the appeal claims and defense opinions of both parties, the issues in dispute in this case are: 1. Whether this case should be stayed; 2. Whether Zhongjin Industrial Company should compensate Qingdao Yuneng Company for losses due to its application for property preservation; 3. How to determine the amount of compensation by Zhongjin Industrial Company; 4. Whether Zhongjin Haoyun Company should bear joint and several liability for compensation. Based on the facts found in this case and the relevant legal provisions, the analysis is as follows:

1. Whether this case should be stayed

Zhongjin Industrial Company appealed and argued that this case should be stayed for two reasons: first, it believed that if the retrial of Shandong High People's Court case (2015) Lu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 39 ultimately determined that it had the right to repurchase Qingdao Yuneng Company's equity, then the property preservation applied for by Zhongjin Industrial Company in Shandong High People's Court case (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2 would not be erroneous; second, after Zhongjin Industrial Company repurchased Qingdao Yuneng Company's equity, the relationship between it and Qingdao Yuneng Company would be that of a parent company and a subsidiary, and the dispute in this case would become pointless due to the alignment of interests. This court holds that Article 150, paragraph 1, item 5 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides that a lawsuit shall be stayed if the trial of the case depends on the result of another case that has not yet been concluded. In this case, first, determining whether the property preservation applied for by Zhongjin Industrial Company in Shandong High People's Court case (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2 was erroneous requires examining whether its litigation conduct in that case was at fault at that time, not whether it still had a right of repurchase after that case. Regardless of whether the final judgment of Shandong High People's Court case (2015) Lu Min Yi Chu Zi No. 39 determines whether it can repurchase Qingdao Yuneng Company's equity, it does not affect the judgment in this case. Second, the compensation for losses determined by the judgment in this case constitutes independent property of Qingdao Yuneng Company, which is not only related to the interests of its shareholders but also involves the interests of Qingdao Yuneng Company's creditors. Even if Zhongjin Industrial Company repurchases the equity and the relationship becomes that of a parent company and a subsidiary, a judgment should still be rendered on the dispute in this case. Therefore, Zhongjin Industrial Company's appeal argument that this case should be stayed cannot be established.

2. Whether Zhongjin Industrial Company should compensate Qingdao Yuneng Company for losses due to its application for property preservation

Zhongjin Industrial Company appealed, arguing that its property preservation conduct was not at fault and lacked subjective malice; Zhongjin Haoyun Company appealed, arguing that Zhongjin Industrial Company did not have the subjective intent or gross negligence to erroneously apply for property preservation to harm the legitimate rights and interests of Qingdao Yuneng Company, and that the court of first instance, by merely concluding that the preservation application was erroneous because Zhongjin Industrial Company's claims were not supported, lacked factual and legal basis. This court holds that Article 100 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "If it may become difficult to enforce a judgment or cause other damage to a party due to the conduct of one party or for other reasons, the people's court may, upon application of the other party, rule to preserve the party's property, order it to perform a certain act, or prohibit it from performing a certain act." Article 105 provides: "If an application is erroneous, the applicant shall compensate the respondent for losses suffered as a result of the preservation." The purpose of the property preservation system is to ensure the enforcement of future effective judgments. Applying for property preservation is an important litigation right of the parties. Although the property preservation ordered by a people's court upon a party's application is a judicial measure taken after a formal review of the application, its premise and basis are the party's application for property preservation. If the improper exercise of the right by the preservation applicant causes property losses to others, the preservation applicant shall bear tort liability for compensation. The determination of tort liability shall apply the provisions of Article 6 of the Tort Liability Law of the People's Republic of China: "If a person infringes upon the civil rights and interests of another person due to fault, he shall bear tort liability." Whether the preservation applicant is at fault should be determined not only by whether its litigation claims are ultimately supported, but also by whether there is intent or gross negligence. Whether the preservation applicant has intent or gross negligence should be determined by examining whether the litigation it filed is reasonable based on the claims and the facts and reasons on which they are based, or by examining whether its application for property preservation is appropriate in light of the amount, object, and method of the preservation sought. If the litigation filed by the preservation applicant is reasonable and the application for property preservation is appropriate, it does not constitute intent or gross negligence; otherwise, there is fault. In this case, first, the lawsuit filed by Zhongjin Industrial Company in Shandong High People's Court case (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2 lacked reasonableness. According to the terms of the "Cooperation Framework Agreement," "Supplemental Agreement," and "Investment Cooperation Agreement," China Railway Company's investment in Qingdao Yuneng Company was to obtain returns from project sales, and the premise for equity repurchase was that China Railway Company had already obtained investment returns during the normal operation period in the agreed proportion. According to the determination of the effective civil judgment of the Supreme People's Court (2011) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 2, the project in question had not yet been sold, the investment risk of China Railway Company in the project had not been fully released, and before the completion of the project's construction and sales, Zhongjin Industrial Company did not have the right to request China Railway Company to immediately fulfill the agreed equity repurchase conditions, and ultimately all of Zhongjin Industrial Company's claims were dismissed. After China Railway Company invested in Qingdao Yuneng Company to promote the project's development and operation but before obtaining returns through project sales, Zhongjin Industrial Company, on the grounds of exercising the equity repurchase right, filed a lawsuit against China Railway Company in Shandong High People's Court case (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2 and demanded huge compensation, which was clearly inconsistent with the parties' agreement on equity repurchase in the contract. Without corresponding evidence that Qingdao Yuneng Company's business conduct clearly harmed the company's interests, Zhongjin Industrial Company listed Qingdao Yuneng Company as a co-defendant and asked it to cease any form of disposal of the project, which lacked factual basis. Second, Zhongjin Industrial Company's litigation preservation conduct lacked appropriateness. On the one hand, when Zhongjin Industrial Company could have frozen Qingdao Yuneng Company's housing sales account to protect its interests after realizing the equity repurchase, it instead took preservation measures to seize the land use right of Qingdao Yuneng Company, preventing the normal sales of the project in question. The object and method of its preservation application were inappropriate. On the other hand, when Qingdao Yuneng Company provided a deposit of RMB 120 million as a guarantee to replace and unseal the project's land use right, Zhongjin Industrial Company repeatedly increased the amount of its claims and the seizure limit in order to counteract Qingdao Yuneng Company's unsealing, causing the project's land use right to remain under seizure for over a year. This preservation conduct was also clearly inappropriate. Therefore, in Shandong High People's Court case (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2, not only were all of Zhongjin Industrial Company's claims dismissed, but also its filing of that lawsuit lacked reasonableness, its application for property preservation measures lacked appropriateness, it was clearly at fault subjectively, and it objectively caused losses to Qingdao Yuneng Company. Pursuant to Article 105 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Zhongjin Industrial Company shall compensate Qingdao Yuneng Company for the losses suffered as a result of its erroneous application for property preservation.

3. How to determine the amount of compensation by Zhongjin Industrial Company

Qingdao Yuneng Company claimed losses in this case in two aspects: first, the interest loss on the RMB 120 million fund provided for replacing the seizure, which was frozen for half a year; second, the interest loss on the house sales proceeds corresponding to the one-year delay in project sales due to the litigation property preservation.

(1) Regarding the interest loss on the RMB 120 million frozen fund of Qingdao Yuneng Company. Zhongjin Industrial Company and Zhongjin Haoyun Company appealed, arguing that Qingdao Yuneng Company was at fault for not timely applying for the lifting of the freeze, that such loss did not exist, and that even if it did, it should be calculated as deposit interest and should be confiscated because it involved illegal lending. This court holds that freezing the funds of the preserved party through property preservation affects the preserved party's use and benefit of the funds, inevitably causing corresponding interest losses, and the preservation applicant shall compensate. If the preserved party provides evidence that the funds were borrowed from others or that a contract to lend them to others was signed before the freeze, the interest loss is the actual loss, but the sum of this interest loss plus the bank interest on the frozen funds shall not exceed the 24% annual interest rate cap stipulated in the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases." Otherwise, the interest loss on the preserved party's funds may be determined by reference to the benchmark loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period, or the standard of 6% annual interest for capital occupation in the absence of agreed term and overdue interest rates under the aforementioned provisions. In this case, first, after Qingdao Yuneng Company provided RMB 120 million to replace the seizure of the project's land use right, Zhongjin Industrial Company increased the litigation claim amount and the preservation limit. It took time for Qingdao Yuneng Company to apply for the lifting of the fund freeze and for the people's court to review and issue a ruling. The claim by Zhongjin Industrial Company and Zhongjin Haoyun Company that Qingdao Yuneng Company was at fault for not timely applying for the lifting of the freeze cannot be established. Second, Qingdao Yuneng Company borrowed RMB 120 million from its shareholder, China Railway Company, to lift the seizure of the project's land use right, which does not violate the laws, regulations, and judicial interpretations concerning private lending. The claim by Zhongjin Industrial Company and Zhongjin Haoyun Company that it should be confiscated because of illegal lending lacks legal basis. Third, as a real estate development enterprise, the freezing of a huge amount of funds of Qingdao Yuneng Company inevitably caused corresponding capital losses. In the contract in question, it was also agreed that China Railway Company would calculate investment returns at 30% of the total investment actually used by Qingdao Yuneng Company each year. The appeal claims by Zhongjin Industrial Company and Zhongjin Haoyun Company that there were no losses and that the loss should be deposit interest are inconsistent with the facts. Therefore, the court of first instance, based on Qingdao Yuneng Company's claim, ordered Zhongjin Industrial Company to compensate Qingdao Yuneng Company for the interest loss of RMB 3.51 million on the RMB 120 million frozen for half a year at the loan interest rate of the People's Bank of China for the same period, which was not improper.

(2) Regarding the loss from delayed project sales. Qingdao Yuneng Company claimed interest for one year based on 30% of the total expected sales amount. The court of first instance discretionarily determined the interest loss for one year based on 10% of its total sales amount. Zhongjin Industrial Company appealed, arguing that even if it had not preserved by seizure, Qingdao Yuneng Company would not have had complete control over the housing sales proceeds, which would have been held in an account, resulting only in deposit interest rates, not loan interest rates. Zhongjin Haoyun Company appealed, arguing that the housing sales of Qingdao Yuneng Company were affected by various factors such as local policies, and that its losses had no causal relationship with the property preservation by Zhongjin Industrial Company; given the continuously rising real estate prices in Qingdao since 2011, the delayed sales of Qingdao Yuneng Company's properties resulted in no loss but rather a profit, and thus the discretionary determination of interest loss on housing sales proceeds by the court of first instance lacked factual basis. This court holds that Article 20 of the "Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Handling of Property Preservation Cases by People's Courts" provides: "During the period of property preservation, the preserved person may request to dispose of the preserved property on its own. If the people's court, upon review, finds that it does not harm the legitimate rights and interests of the preservation applicant and other executing creditors, it may permit it, but shall supervise the preserved person to dispose of the property at a reasonable price within a specified period and control the corresponding proceeds. If the preserved person requests to dispose of the preserved property that is the subject of the dispute on its own, the consent of the preservation applicant is required. If the people's court permits the preserved person to dispose of the preserved property on its own, it shall notify the preservation applicant; if the preservation applicant dissents, it may raise an objection in accordance with Article 225 of the Civil Procedure Law." The compensation for erroneous property preservation covers the actual losses of the preserved person, and such losses must have a direct causal relationship with the conduct of the preservation applicant. Pursuant to the aforementioned judicial interpretation, the preserved person has the right to choose whether to dispose of the preserved property. If the preserved person does not make a request, or if its request is improper and not approved by the people's court, the depreciation in value of the preserved property due to market changes is a risk that the preserved person should bear itself and has no direct causal relationship with the preservation application conduct. However, if the preservation applicant does not consent to the preserved person's self-disposition, the property losses suffered by the preserved person due to its inability to exercise the right of disposition have a direct causal relationship with the conduct of the preservation applicant, and in the event of erroneous property preservation, the preservation applicant shall bear corresponding compensation liability. The actual loss of the preserved person should be the price difference between the preserved property at the beginning and end of the preservation, plus the interest loss on the funds corresponding to the price at the beginning. In this case, first, Qingdao Yuneng Company raised RMB 120 million to replace the seizure of the project's land use right in order to sell the houses, but Zhongjin Industrial Company continuously increased the litigation claim amount and the seizure limit. Its erroneous property preservation conduct prevented Qingdao Yuneng Company from selling the houses. It shall compensate Qingdao Yuneng Company for the actual losses suffered during this period. The appeal reasons by Zhongjin Industrial Company and Zhongjin Haoyun Company, arguing that there was no causal relationship between the preservation seizure and the housing sales loss, and that Qingdao Yuneng Company was grossly negligent for failing to exercise its preservation reconsideration right and take measures to replace the seizure to reduce losses, cannot be established. Second, the court of first instance discretionarily determined the loss from delayed project sales to be compensated by Zhongjin Industrial Company based on 10% of Qingdao Yuneng Company's total sales amount as the base, with interest calculated at the same-period bank loan interest rate, which had corresponding factual and legal basis. Although Zhongjin Industrial Company and Zhongjin Haoyun Company claimed that real estate prices in Qingdao had continuously risen since 2011, they did not provide evidence to prove that the difference between the actual sales price or market value of 10% of the project's houses at the end of the seizure and the expected sales price at the beginning of the seizure, minus the financing loss on the expected sales price of Qingdao Yuneng Company's 10% project houses at the beginning of the seizure during the period of erroneous preservation, was greater than the interest loss on the housing sales proceeds determined discretionarily by the court of first instance. Therefore, the appeal claim by Zhongjin Industrial Company and Zhongjin Haoyun Company that Qingdao Yuneng Company suffered no loss from the delayed sale of its properties and thus no compensation is needed also cannot be established. The court of first instance's discretionary determination that Zhongjin Industrial Company should compensate Qingdao Yuneng Company for the interest loss of RMB 63,184,624.35 from the delayed project sales was not improper, and this court upholds it.

4. Whether Zhongjin Haoyun Company should bear joint and several liability for compensation

Zhongjin Haoyun Company appealed, arguing that its guarantee was invalid due to lack of a shareholders' resolution, and that even if it should bear liability, it should only be liable to the extent of the property provided as security, not as joint and several guarantee liability. We hold that a guarantee provided for property preservation is a judicial guarantee issued to the people's court, not a guarantee between equal civil parties. Property preservation measures are taken upon application; if property preservation is erroneous, the applicant for preservation is the tortfeasor. If a third party provides a guarantee, it shall bear corresponding guarantee liability for the losses of the preserved party in accordance with its commitment. In this case, first, the guarantee provided by Zhongjin Haoyun Company in the case Shandong High People's Court (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2 was legally effective after being examined and accepted by that court. Zhongjin Haoyun Company's appellate argument that its guarantee was invalid due to lack of a shareholders' resolution lacks legal basis. Second, in the case Shandong High People's Court (2011) Lu Shang Chu Zi No. 2, the party that committed the erroneous property preservation was Zhongjin Industrial Company, not Zhongjin Haoyun Company. Zhongjin Haoyun Company's provision of the preservation guarantee for Zhongjin Industrial Company does not constitute a joint tort. The first instance judgment, which found that Zhongjin Haoyun Company and Zhongjin Industrial Company constituted a joint tort and imposed joint and several compensatory liability under Article 8 of the Tort Law of the People's Republic of China, was an erroneous application of law, and we hereby correct it. Third, the three Property Preservation Guarantee Letters issued by Zhongjin Haoyun Company clearly stated that it would use its property at No. 192 Duxin Shimao Plaza, east of Binhai Shiqi Road and south of Huanghe Qi Road, Binzhou City, as property security for the preservation of Zhongjin Industrial Company, and that if losses were caused to the preserved party due to improper preservation, it would bear corresponding liability. Therefore, it should bear guarantee liability within the value of the secured property. The guarantee letters issued by Zhongjin Haoyun Company did not express an intention to assume unlimited joint and several liability, and Qingdao Yulong Company's argument that Zhongjin Haoyun Company should bear joint and several liability in accordance with the commitment in the guarantee letters is inconsistent with the facts.

Furthermore, based on the issues in dispute in this case and the facts found, the participation or non-participation of China Railway Company and Rongzhidi Company in the lawsuit does not affect the trial of this case, nor is the outcome of this case related to China Railway Company or Rongzhidi Company. In the second instance, Zhongjin Industrial Company applied to add China Railway Company and Rongzhidi Company as defendants or third parties, which lacks factual and legal basis and is hereby not supported. In addition, according to the analysis above, apart from the guarantee letters issued by Zhongjin Haoyun Company, other new evidence submitted by the parties in the second instance is not relevant to the facts and the determination of the disputed issues in this case, and shall not be admitted.

In conclusion, the appellate claims of Zhongjin Industrial Company cannot be sustained and are hereby dismissed; the appellate claims of Zhongjin Haoyun Company are partially sustained. Pursuant to paragraph 1, item 2 of Article 170 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, we hereby adjudge as follows:

1. Affirm item 1 and item 3 of the civil judgment (2014) Lu Min Yi Chong Chu Zi No. 1 of the Shandong High People's Court;

2. Amend item 2 of the civil judgment (2014) Lu Min Yi Chong Chu Zi No. 1 of the Shandong High People's Court to: Qingdao Zhongjin Yulong Real Estate Co., Ltd. has the right to be compensated on a priority basis from the proceeds from the discount, auction, or sale of the property at No. 192 Duxin Shimao Plaza, east of Binhai Shiqi Road and south of Huanghe Qi Road, Binzhou City, owned by Binzhou Zhongjin Haoyun Real Estate Co., Ltd., to the extent of the creditor's rights determined in item 1 of this judgment.

Court acceptance fee for the first instance: RMB 1,007,119, to be borne by Qingdao Zhongjin Yulong Real Estate Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 671,413, and jointly by Qingdao Zhongjin Industrial Co., Ltd. and Binzhou Zhongjin Haoyun Real Estate Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 335,706; property preservation fee: RMB 5,000, to be borne by Qingdao Zhongjin Yulong Real Estate Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 2,500, and jointly by Qingdao Zhongjin Industrial Co., Ltd. and Binzhou Zhongjin Haoyun Real Estate Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 2,500. Court acceptance fee for the second instance: RMB 1,007,119, to be jointly borne by Qingdao Zhongjin Industrial Co., Ltd. and Binzhou Zhongjin Haoyun Real Estate Co., Ltd.
